truths: Any authenticated doctor can read finalised encounters, prescriptions, timelines, treatment plans, and sessions written by any doctor in the hospital
Reading a clinical record authored by another doctor automatically records a CROSS_DOCTOR_CLINICAL_READ audit entry in audit_logs
A doctor attempting to edit, finalise, add addenda, or cancel another doctor's clinical record is rejected with HTTP 404
Reception and Admin roles attempting to read clinical encounters, clinical notes, or prescriptions are rejected with HTTP 404
All 19 scattered inline doctor_id checks across the 5 clinical routers are eliminated in favor of centralized core/scope.py evaluation

artifacts.provides: Centralized CLINICAL_READ and CLINICAL_WRITE scopes with cross-doctor audit logging
Automated regression tests for cross-doctor read allowance, audit logging, write denial, and reception/admin denial

truths: A consultation loads the approved clinical template version for its department (Physiotherapy or Ophthalmology)
Template responses are persisted per encounter and locked against edits once the encounter is finalised
A new template version never modifies the schema or responses of historical encounters
Doctor can record vitals with height and weight, and the server automatically calculates and stores BMI rounded to 1 decimal place
Vitals values are strictly validated against physiological range limits on both database and API layers

artifacts.provides: Tables for clinical_templates, clinical_template_versions, clinical_template_responses, and vital_observations
Automated tests for template retrieval, seed verification, response persistence, and finalisation validation
Automated tests for vitals recording, server-side BMI computation, and physiological boundary checks

truths: From an empty kalyan_test schema, alembic upgrade head run as kalyan_owner creates doctors, users, sessions, login_throttle, audit_logs, system_setup and alembic_version; audit.record() then writes one audit_logs row inside the caller's transaction and the row disappears when that transaction rolls back (tracer: migration, model, service, real PostgreSQL)

audit_logs rejects UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE for kalyan_app with permission denied and for kalyan_owner through triggers whose message contains append-only (row trigger for UPDATE/DELETE, separate statement trigger for TRUNCATE) (AUD-01)

audit.record() flushes and fails closed (an invalid row raises and leaves nothing after rollback) and raises AuditPayloadError when before/after (including nested dicts) contain password, password_hash, new_password, current_password, token or csrf_token

A fresh migration creates zero users and zero doctors: the migrated_db fixture asserts and records both counts immediately after upgrade head, before any test runs (SEC-05: no seed or default credentials)
users.role has a named CHECK limited to ADMIN, RECEPTION, DOCTOR and a named CHECK that doctor_id is non-null exactly when role is DOCTOR (SEC-03); username is UNIQUE and stored lowercase

0001 grants kalyan_app only: USAGE on schema public; SELECT, INSERT on audit_logs and system_setup; SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE on users, doctors, login_throttle; SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on sessions; SELECT on alembic_version; never DELETE on users, never CREATE on the schema

system_setup is the authoritative setup-completed state (SEC-07): id SMALLINT PRIMARY KEY with named CHECK (id = 1) so at most one row can ever exist, completed_at timestamptz NOT NULL, admin_user_id BIGINT NOT NULL FK to users ON DELETE RESTRICT; it is append-only like audit_logs (row trigger blocking UPDATE/DELETE, statement trigger blocking TRUNCATE, kalyan_app has only SELECT, INSERT); a second INSERT raises a unique violation; a fresh migration has no row
Every mutable table (users, doctors) carries version_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 (D-08); all instants are timestamptz

truths: SC6-1 no users -> available: with no system_setup row, GET /api/setup/status returns 200 {setup_required: true} and the /setup flow can be completed (test_setup_available_when_never_completed)
SC6-2 invalid code -> rejected: a wrong code returns 403 setup_code_invalid, creates nothing, is persisted as a SETUP_CODE_REJECTED audit row and a per-address failure (test_invalid_code_rejected)

SC6-3 valid code -> exactly one admin: the valid code plus username, full name and a policy-compliant password creates one ADMIN (must_change_password false) AND the singleton system_setup row (id 1, completed_at, admin_user_id) in ONE transaction, writes ADMIN_BOOTSTRAPPED with actor setup:wizard, returns 201, and the admin then signs in (tracer; test_valid_code_creates_exactly_one_admin)

SC6-4 two simultaneous valid submissions -> exactly one success: pg_advisory_xact_lock is the first line, the system_setup check is repeated inside the transaction, and the PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1) of system_setup is the database-level guarantee (a duplicate insert maps to 410 setup_closed); a two-thread real-commit test sees [201, 410] and exactly one new ADMIN row (test_simultaneous_submissions_single_admin, marker concurrency)

SC6-5 admin exists -> every setup endpoint rejects, including direct API calls: once a system_setup row exists, GET /api/setup/status and POST /api/setup/admin (any body, any identity, any code) return 410 setup_closed, checked before the code; deactivating every admin later does NOT reopen setup because the gate is the system_setup row, not the active-admin count (test_setup_closed_after_completion, test_setup_not_reopened_by_deactivation, matrix rows)

SC6-6 restart -> stays disabled: after setup a fresh app instance (lifespan run) reports 410, issues no code and creates no code file; before setup a restart issues a new code and the old code no longer works (test_restart_after_setup_stays_closed, test_restart_before_setup_rotates_code)

SC6-7 code never in responses or logs: the code is written only to backend/var/setup-code.txt (git-ignored, outside served paths) and printed to the console with print() only when sys.stdout.isatty() is true; otherwise only a banner naming the file path is printed; the logging module never receives it; caplog over startup, wrong code and right code, every response body and header of the setup endpoints and errors, and every audit row are free of the code (test_code_never_logged, test_code_never_in_responses

Consumption is atomic with creation: the in-memory code hash is cleared and the code file deleted by a response background task that runs only after the transaction committed; if the commit fails the code stays valid (test_failed_commit_does_not_consume_code)

Brute force: after SETUP_LOCK_THRESHOLD (5) wrong codes from one address within SETUP_LOCK_MINUTES (15) that address gets 429 too_many_attempts with Retry-After for the rest of the window (temporary lockout); every failure also feeds the login_throttle table; after 10 wrong codes in total the code is rotated (test_address_locked_after_wrong_codes, test_code_rotated_after_total_failures)

Both setup routes carry the public marker, are in PUBLIC_ALLOWLIST and MUST_EXIST of the route walk and in the role x endpoint matrix (with a system_setup row present every identity gets 410); POST is subject to the Origin==Host check

create-admin is dropped; reset-admin-password is the only recovery path, authenticated by OS-level access to the server PC plus the protected backend/.env database credentials; it only resets an existing active ADMIN, never creates a first admin and never touches or reopens setup (system_setup untouched)

A fresh migration still has zero users and no system_setup row; the legacy default admin pair is absent from backend/ and frontend/; login with it is 401; backend/.env.example password keys are CHANGE_ME; backend/var/setup-code.txt is git-ignored (ROADMAP SC-4)

key-decisions: Hot backups use SQLite's native Connection.backup() to prevent database locks or corruption.
Restoration follows a fail-safe 4-step pipeline: pre-verify -> safety snapshot -> copy -> post-verify.

Pre-restore integrity verification and safe restore pipeline

System generates timestamped backups in data/backups/ (e.g. kalyan_backup_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.db).
Integrity verification tests PRAGMA integrity_check and validates patient/case/payment record counts.
Restore pipeline tests backup file in isolated scratch DB before replacing active database, maintaining safety rollback snapshot.
BackupView UI provides 1-click backup creation, backup history table, and verified restore with confirmation modal.
MainWindow connects sidebar index 4 to live BackupView.
Automated tests in tests/test_backup_service.py achieve 100% assertions pass rate.
AuthService provides PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 password hashing with 100,000+ iterations and cryptographic per-user salting.
System seeds a default administrator account if users table is empty, allowing immediate local administration.
AdminAuthDialog modal prompts and verifies administrator password before dangerous clinic actions (e.g., database restoration).
Database restore action in BackupView is guarded by AdminAuthDialog.
System functions 100% offline with zero outbound network calls, telemetry, or remote dependencies.

truths: An Administrator creates a user via POST /api/users: the 201 response carries a random temporary password exactly once (Cache-Control no-store), the user has must_change_password true and can sign in with it but is held in the change-password flow (tracer; SEC-05)

The temporary password has settings.temp_password_length characters (default 12, EG-19) from an unambiguous alphabet via secrets, passes the policy, and never appears in GET responses, audit rows or logs; USER_CREATED stores role, full_name and doctor_id only

Creating a DOCTOR user requires doctor_name_en and inserts the stub doctor and the user in one transaction; ADMIN/RECEPTION with doctor_name_en is 422; duplicate usernames (case-insensitive) are 409 username_taken
Request models use extra=forbid: password_hash, failed_login_count, is_active, version_id (on create), locked_until are 422 (no mass assignment)
Every versioned entity JSON carries version_id; every update body carries version_id (required, >= 1, missing 422) (D-08)
A stale update returns 409 {code version_conflict, message 'Record was modified by another user', entity, id} with Cache-Control no-store; row and audit unchanged (D-08, SEC-06)
The service compares the client's version_id with the loaded entity (require_version); version_id_col alone is not relied on, and no code assigns the version_id attribute from input
The response is built after session.flush() so it carries version_id previous + 1

Two parallel PATCHes with the same version_id give exactly one 200 and one 409 in 20 of 20 iterations on real PostgreSQL (concurrency marker, run at wave end and in the 11-16 gate), and a deterministic two-session race raises StaleDataError mapped to the same 409

Role change only between ADMIN and RECEPTION (to or from DOCTOR is 409 role_change_not_allowed, EG-15); own role change 409 self_action_forbidden; demoting the last active admin 409 last_admin; USER_ROLE_CHANGED and USER_UPDATED audited with changed-field diffs
A failed login (Core UPDATE, 11-06) between GET and PATCH does not change version_id

artifacts.provides: GET /api/users, GET /api/users/{id}, POST /api/users, PATCH /api/users/{id}
create_user, update_user, generate_temp_password
Stale 409, races, no-assignment scan

prohibitions.statement: Must NOT assign version_id from request input
Must NOT expose a DELETE route for users
Must NOT return password_hash, tokens or the temporary password outside the one-time create response
Must NOT silently overwrite or auto-retry a stale update

key-decisions: Monetary values stored strictly in integer paise (1 INR = 100 paise) preventing IEEE 754 float drift.
Sessions are sequentially numbered per case and chronologically ordered (session_number ASC, session_timestamp ASC).
Payments <= 0 are rejected; overpayments flag is_overpayment while clamping balance to 0.

coverage.description: Treatment case creation and chronological session logging
Integer paise currency arithmetic and balance calculation

truths: TreatmentView displays patient treatment cases, progress badge (completed/target sessions), and chronological session timeline.
Add Session dialog allows clinicians to log dated notes, therapist name, treatment modalities, and pain score (0-10).
PaymentView displays agreed fee, total paid, and dynamic outstanding balance card with currency-safe integer paise arithmetic.
Recording a payment immediately updates the balance ledger and payment history table.
MainWindow connects sidebar navigation index 2 ('Treatment Cases') and index 3 ('Billing & Payments') with live data views.
Automated UI tests in tests/test_treatment_ui.py verify session dialog logging and payment balance updates.
key_links: main_window.py integrates treatment_view.py at index 2 and payment_view.py at index 3.

truths: System provides TreatmentRepository for parameterized CRUD on treatment_cases and chronological treatment_sessions.
System provides PaymentRepository for recording installments and querying ledger records.
BillingService operates strictly in integer paise (1 INR = 100 paise), guaranteeing zero floating-point rounding errors.
BillingService automatically computes Balance = Total Fee - Sum(Payments), rejects negative/zero payments, and flags overpayments.
TreatmentService validates pain scores (0-10), requires non-empty clinical notes, and assigns strictly incrementing session numbers.
Comprehensive automated tests in tests/test_billing_service.py and tests/test_treatment_service.py achieve 100% assertion pass rate.

truths: Migration 0018 creates patient_import_batches and patient_import_rows staging tables
The 8-stage pipeline progresses in exact order: Upload -> Inspect -> Map -> Validate -> Resolve -> Preview -> Commit -> Reconcile
Every imported patient receives a newly minted gap-free URN (KH-YYYY-XXXX); old numbers are recorded in legacy_urn
URN allocation occurs strictly during the commit transaction for committed rows, preventing any URN sequence gaps from failed rows
Pre-commit safety backup runs automatically via backup_service; if the backup fails, commit aborts immediately without modifying patients
Importing never updates or overwrites existing patients; duplicate candidates are resolved explicitly as 'Skip' (default) or 'Import as New'
Rows missing required fields (guardian, gender, age, mobile, address) do not block valid rows from committing and are downloadable as error CSV in Reconcile stage
Staged and committed batches write PATIENT_IMPORT_STAGED and PATIENT_IMPORT_COMMITTED audit events

truths: A user with must_change_password true can sign in, but every permission-protected route returns 403 password_change_required; only GET /api/auth/me, POST /api/auth/logout and POST /api/auth/change-password work until the password is changed (tracer; SEC-05)

Password policy numbers are Settings, not code constants (EG-19): password_min_length 10, password_max_length 128 and temp_password_length 12 with KALYAN_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH, KALYAN_PASSWORD_MAX_LENGTH, KALYAN_TEMP_PASSWORD_LENGTH overrides; a validator keeps min >= 8 and max <= 1024; only the blocklist word list is code

change-password requires the current password, applies the policy (min/max from Settings, not equal to username or full name case-insensitively, not in the embedded blocklist of at least 100 entries, no composition rules), sets must_change_password false and password_changed_at, revokes ALL the user's sessions and returns a fresh cookie and csrf_token
A wrong current password returns 403 current_password_invalid, counts toward the lockout counter, and persists because the response is returned
AUTH_PASSWORD_CHANGED stores only the must_change_password transition; AUTH_PASSWORD_CHANGE_FAILED is written for wrong current passwords; no password text appears in audit rows

Every unsafe request (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE), including login, needs an Origin (else Referer) whose host:port equals the Host header or matches KALYAN_EXTRA_ALLOWED_ORIGINS; null or missing is 403 csrf_failed; GET and HEAD are unaffected (SEC-02 CSRF under D-01)
Every authenticated unsafe request must carry X-CSRF-Token equal to its own session's token (hmac.compare_digest), else 403 csrf_failed
verify_origin is the only app-level dependency; authentication and permission checks are never global

truths.statement: Browsers send Origin on same-origin unsafe fetches over plain HTTP, otherwise the Referer fallback carries the check (A16); confirmed in the 11-16 manual UAT

truths: Starting a consultation for an appointment with an existing encounter reopens that encounter rather than creating a duplicate
A consultation draft can be saved with partial or empty symptoms, clinical notes, and diagnosis, returning 200/201 and updating version_id
Finalising a consultation strictly validates that chief complaint (symptoms) and diagnosis are non-empty
Reception checking in a patient records the exact check_in_at timestamp on the appointment
A user attempting to log in when an active, unexpired session exists is rejected with 409 session_in_use unless takeover=True is supplied
A session takeover immediately revokes prior sessions for that user and records a SESSION_TAKEOVER audit event
